added: Sorting laundry may be a little bit of a pain, but it's a great way to keep your clothes looking snappy. If you don't want your tie-dye t-shirt to ruin your favorite white dress, sorting your clothes by color is what you've gotta do. Here are some helpful tips to organize your laundry and make the process run smoothly. Your pristine wardrobe will make it all worth it.
===Designate laundry piles.===

#How many you make will depend on the colors of your wardrobe. Separating whites, lights, and darks is a must. If you really want to protect your clothes, try adding a pile for bright colors like reds and oranges. Grab another for delicate items, plus one more for denim.<ref>https://youtu.be/YfmCwtOg0UY?t=39</ref> [[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Store each pile in a separate hamper to make the process more organized!
===Grab all of your white clothes and put them in their hamper.===

#This means clothing that is pure white. The clothes shouldn't contain any designs, labels, or patterns. These clothes can be bleached with chlorine bleach, as they don't contain any other colors and won't be damaged in the process.<ref>https://youtu.be/YfmCwtOg0UY?t=158</ref> You can wash these in hot water and dry them at a high temperature.<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Pick one for lights.===

#Put white items with labels or designs in this container. You should also include pastel colors like light yellow, light green, pink, and yellow. Wash these items in warm water and dry them at a warm temperature.<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>
#*Throw in khakis and light blues in this hamper, too!
===Gather all of your dark clothes.===

#This includes clothes that are black, dark gray, blue, and purple. You can also include jeans in this category. Include red and orange (unless you want to separate bright colors from dark colors). Wash these in cold water and dry them at a low temperature.<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Seperate bright colors from dark colors to be extra careful.===

#Throw in reds, pinks, and oranges. These items are the most likely to bleed during the washing cycle, so it's a good idea to wash them separately if you have the time. Wash these items in cold water and dry them at a low temperature.<ref>http://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Seperate your jeans if you really want to be safe.===

#Denim has a tendency to bleed during the first few washing cycles. Wash denim clothes like jeans, jean jackets, and other pieces to ensure that there's no dye transfer. Put all of your denim clothes together and wash them in cold to warm water. When drying, dry them on medium heat, as hotter temperatures can wear down and fade the denim.<ref>http://www.esquire.com/style/advice/a44472/how-to-wash-your-jeans/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Wash your jeans inside out to prevent the color from fading. You don't want those chic dark-wash jeans to become light-wash jeans after a few washes!
#*To really preserve the color of your denim clothes, hand wash and air dry them.
===Set aside delicates like lace items, bras, and underwear.===

#This also includes anything with trim, beading, or sequins. Be sure to check the label before putting these clothes in the washer or dryer. They may need to be hand washed or air-dried. If not, choose the delicates cycle if your washer has one, and dry them on low to prevent damage.<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-choose-the-washing-cycle/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*You should also include crochet fabrics and pantyhose in this pile.
#*Consider using a delicates bag to give your clothes extra protection in the washer and dryer.<ref>https://youtu.be/02hHPF4M88M?t=195</ref>
===Make an extra sorting pile for stained clothes.===

#Some clothes may need special cleaning solution prior to washing. If you recently spilled breakfast cereal on your favorite shirt and got grass stains on your jeans (it happens to the best of us!), make a separate pile for stained clothing while you sort. Spray the clothes with stain removal spray or apply a stain remover pen. After, put each clothing item in their designated pile (whites, light colors, dark colors, etc.).<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>
#*You can also [[Remove-Set-in-Stains|remove stains]] using vinegar or a mixture of  {{convert|4|tbsp|mL}} baking soda and {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of water.
===Go the extra mile and isolate cotton fabrics.===

#Sort your clothes by fabric to keep them in excellent condition. Gather all of your cotton clothes and wash and dry them separately. Cotton is thinner than many other fabrics, so it doesn't need as much time to dry. Don't dry cotton with other materials, as you may risk overheating them. Ensure your cotton t-shirt doesn't shrink by drying it with only other cotton fabrics!<ref>http://www.goodhousekeeping.com/home/cleaning/tips/a24173/sorting-laundry/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Keep acrylic, polyester, and nylon together.===

#These fabrics are synthetic and can be washed and dried together. Wash and dry them on the permanent press cycle. This cycle is powerful enough to clean your clothes, but keeps a slower spin to avoid wrinkles.<ref>https://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-choose-the-washing-cycle/</ref> If your washer and dryer doesn't include this cycle, wash them in cold to warm water and dry them on low heat.<ref>https://www.whowhatwear.com/how-to-wash-polyester/slide4</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid washing and drying nylon and polyester on high heat, as these fabrics tend to shrink.
===Keep new clothing items in their own pile.===

#Wash and dry new clothing items on their own to see how they react. Clothing items like brightly-colored sweaters or a new pair of jeans may bleed or damage other clothes in the washing and drying cycle. They may not, though! Test out how they react by washing and drying them on their own. When sorting your laundry, keep new clothing items separate to keep the rest of your clothes safe.<ref>https://youtu.be/YfmCwtOg0UY?t=220</ref>

#*For example, let's say you just got a cute white blouse with a purple design on the front. Wash it alone and check if the water turns purple or becomes discolored. If it doesn't, that shirt is probably safe to wash with other light colors!
removed: Sorting your laundry will prevent items from being ruined when dye bleeds out during the wash cycle. Separating your clothes by color, such as whites, lights, brights, and darks, before washing will help keep your clothes in tip-top shape. You can even separate further and wash similar fabrics together (such as only denim in one load, cotton in another), wash synthetics separately, and remove delicates for hand-washing.
===Sorting Whites, Lights and Darks===

#Designate laundry containers. You’ll want three to six laundry baskets, bags, or hampers. The number will depend on the colors in your wardrobe: separating by whites, lights, and darks is a must, but you could also add one for bright colors such as reds and oranges, one for delicate items, or even one for just denim items. Put items in their designated container as soon as you remove them.[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Choose one for whites. This basket or container will be for white clothing only. This means clothing that is pure white; it should not contain any designs, labels, insignias, or patterns. These items can be bleached with chlorine bleach since they do not contain any other colors. Wash white clothing in hot water, and dry at a high temperature.<ref>http://lancaster.unl.edu/home/articles/2007/laundrysort.shtml</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Pick one for lights. Add light-colored clothing only to this basket. Put white items with labels or designs in this container, as well as other light-colored items such as khakis or pastel items. Wash light-colored clothing in warm water, and dry them at a warm temperature.<ref>http://lancaster.unl.edu/home/articles/2007/laundrysort.shtml</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Select one for darks. Dark clothing includes jeans as well as black, dark gray, blue, and purple items. Depending on the colors in your wardrobe and the way you choose to sort, red and orange items could be added to the dark container as well. Dark-colored laundry should be washed in cold water, and dried at a low temperature.<ref>http://lancaster.unl.edu/home/articles/2007/laundrysort.shtml</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Sorting Other Colors===

#Use a separate container for brights. Bright colored clothing includes reds, pinks, and oranges. These items are the most likely to bleed when washing, so it is a good idea to wash them separately from other items. Bright-colored laundry should be washed in cold water, and dried at a low temperature.<ref>http://www.mamaslaundrytalk.com/laundry-basics-how-to-sort-clothes/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Separate your jeans. Denim often bleeds when washing it, especially the first few times. The fabric is also heavier than many other clothing items. You can wash denim items separately from your other clothing to ensure there is no dye transfer, and dry them together to prevent other items from being heated too long. Washing your jeans inside out also helps preserve the color as well as clean the dirtiest part: the inside.<ref>http://www.esquire.com/style/advice/a44472/how-to-wash-your-jeans/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Set aside delicates. Delicate items may include clothing with special trim, beading, sequins, or lace, as well as underwear, bras, or nightgowns. These items should be washed separately from your other clothes, and be sure to check the labels before putting them in the washer or dryer. You may need to hand wash these items and hang them up or lay them flat to dry.<ref>http://lancaster.unl.edu/home/articles/2007/laundrysort.shtml</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Using Fabric to Sort===

#Isolate cotton fabrics. Cotton is thinner than many other fabrics, meaning it does not need to dry as long. Washing and drying cotton items together will prevent the fabric from being over-stressed, as all your items should be dry at the same time. Cotton can also withstand higher temperatures than other fabrics, and can be washed in hot water and dried at a high temperature.<ref>http://www.goodhousekeeping.com/home/cleaning/tips/a24173/sorting-laundry/</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Separate linens. Linen fabric is often more absorbent as well as more delicate than other kinds of clothing. Washing linen items together will ensure your clothing stays in good condition. Wash and dry linen fabrics at low temperatures to avoid shrinkage.<ref>https://www.thelaundress.com/How-To/Linen.html</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Keep acrylic, polyester, and nylon together. These fabrics are synthetic and can be washed and dried together. Synthetic fabrics such as acrylic, polyester, and nylon are pretty durable and can be washed and dried at high temperatures. Remember to turn the temp down if these items are dark in color though, as lower heat helps keep the color from fading.<ref>http://laundry.reviewed.com/features/the-ultimate-guide-to-fabrics-and-how-to-clean-them</ref>[[Image:Sort Laundry by Colors Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]
*New items like bright-colored sweaters and jeans should be washed separately the first few times to ensure the dye doesn’t bleed onto your other clothes.

Synthetic fabrics such as acrylic, polyester, and nylon are pretty durable and can be washed and dried at high temperatures. Remember to turn the temp down if these items are dark in color though, as lower heat helps keep the color from fading.<ref>http://laundry.reviewed.com/features/the-ultimate-guide-to-fabrics-and-how-to-clean-them</ref>

#Separate your jeans. Denim often bleeds when washing it, especially the first few times. The fabric is also heavier than many other clothing items. You can wash denim items separately from your other clothing to ensure there is no dye transfer, and dry them together to prevent other items from being heated too long. Washing your jeans inside out also helps preserve the color as well as clean the dirtiest part: the inside.<ref>http://www.esquire.com/style/advice/a44472/how-to-wash-your-jeans/</ref>

#Set aside delicates. Delicate items may include clothing with special trim, beading, sequins, or lace, as well as underwear, bras, or nightgowns. These items should be washed separately from your other clothes, and be sure to check the labels before putting them in the washer or dryer. You may need to hand wash these items and hang them up or lay them flat to dry.<ref>http://lancaster.unl.edu/home/articles/2007/laundrysort.shtml</ref>

== Tips ==

*Don't use dryer sheets too often because the dryer sheets aren't very good for clothes especially towels. Since the dryer sheets will not let the towel absorb a lot of the water when you dry yourself after taking a nice long shower.
*Don't leave your clothes in the washer or dryer unattended because obviously people will want to steal your clothes especially if they like the shirt or jeans, pants etc.
*Don't go ahead and throw all of your clothes (whites, dark colors and light colors) together because dark colors may "bleed" onto your whites.

*If you leave clothes unattended in the dryer... people will probably change the temp.  Like if you leave the temperature on a low setting, someone might change it to high temp setting and then you will be stuck wearing tight clothes.  Or you will have to throw them out.
== Warnings ==
*DO NOT leave your laundry unattended because someone might see a nice shirt or t-shirt and they would steal it after the load is done and you didn't come and pick it up.
*Also, DON'T OVER LOAD THE WASHERS!
*If the dryer has some burnt smell, DON'T USE IT! just find another dryer and use that instead.
*Only use bleach on WHITES.  Chlorine bleach is for WHITES only, and Oxygen Bleach is safe for Colors.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Dirty clothes
*Bag
*Washer/Dryer
*Stain treaters
*Detergent
*Dryer sheets (optional)

== Steps ==
#Start by putting out all of your clothes onto the ground or on your bed.

#*  Try to find 3-4 washers that are free and are right beside each other.  That way you won't have to worry about walking all around the entire laundromat just to put your clothes in.

#*Whites will need to be washed in hot water with bleach (optional) and detergent.  Light colors should be washed in either cold or warm depending on what you think is better.  Dark colors should be washed in cold water because dark colors may bleed.
#*  It is best to spray a stain treater on them such as Spray n' Wash, or Shout.

#Then put the desired amount of detergent into the detergent dispenser and then put in your quarters, or loonies depending on what the machines will accept.  Usually laundromats close to College, or in the dorm rooms usually take quarters.  Other than that, you will need to have loonies.  Also, DON'T OVER LOAD THE WASHERS! and DO NOT leave your laundry unattended because someone might see a nice shirt or t-shirt and they would steal it after the load is done and you didn't come and pick it up.

#*When all of your loads are done, check if your stains that you treated are gone.  If not, you will want to rewash it.  If you have many garments that are stained, you can wash them all again.  Just make sure that if you have whites and colors but are fairly small, you can just put them all in the same machine just on COLD.  Then all of the other nice and clean clothes, you can go ahead and throw them into the dryer.

#*When you get to the dryer, just to be sure, put your dark colors on a medium temp or high temp if you have a large load of dark colors.  If you have light colors, a warm setting or high heat setting will be good.  If you have whites.  It is best you dry them all at a high heat temperature.

#When the clothes are done being dried in the dryer, it is best to take ALL the clothes out immediately to prevent wrinkling.  Especially if you have nice dress shirts, or nice shirts that you want to wear.  Otherwise you will have to iron or steam the shirt..

#*Don't forget about your other clothes that were stained and were rewashed again!  If you don't want to use more money on drying the clothes (if the stains are gone) then you can just take them with you and then if you have hangers, or a drying rack then you can hang them inside or outside (if you have a balcony) and then after that.  You can just fold or hang your clothes.  Then you are done!
== Tips ==
*Don't go ahead and throw all of your clothes (whites, dark colors and light colors) together because dark colors may "bleed" onto your whites.

*Don't use dryer sheets too often because the dryer sheets aren't very good for clothes especially towels.  Since the dryer sheets will not let the towel absorb a lot of the water when you dry yourself after taking a nice long shower.
*Don't leave your clothes in the washer or dryer unattended because obviously people will want to steal your clothes especially if they like the shirt or jeans, pants etc.

*Other than that, if you leave clothes unattended in the dryer... people will probably change the temp.  Like if you leave the temperature on a low setting, someone might change it to high temp setting and then you will be stuck wearing tight clothes.  Or you will have to throw them out.
== Warnings ==
*If the dryer has some burnt smell, DON'T USE IT! just find another dryer and use that instead.
*Only use bleach on WHITES.  Chlorine bleach is for WHITES only, and Oxygen Bleach is safe for Colors.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Dirty clothes
*Bag
*Washer/Dryer
*Stain treaters
*Detergent
*Dryer sheets (optional)
